q: In a period, the properties of transition elements are very similar in contrast to those of s-block and ____ elements.
e: Transition elements show less variation in properties across a period compared to s- and p-block elements.

q: This is because, in a transition series, the valence shell electron configuration of the elements does not ____.
e: The outermost s-orbital electron configuration remains relatively constant across a transition series.

q: These transition elements have typical metallic properties such as malleability, ductility, metallic lustre, and high ____ strength.
e: Transition metals are characterized by high tensile strength and other typical metallic properties.

q: They are silvery-white except for ____, which is brownish-red in colour.
e: Copper is distinct among 3d transition metals due to its brownish-red colour.

q: One cubic centimetre ($1 cm^3$) cube of iron is ____ times heavier than a $1 cm^3$ cube of sodium.
e: Transition metals have a much higher density compared to alkali metals like sodium.

q: Transition elements are significantly less reactive than Group ____ metals.
e: Transition metals are much less reactive than the highly reactive Group I alkali metals.

q: For example, nickel and copper do not react with water, or catch fire in the air (oxygen), unlike ____.
e: Sodium reacts vigorously with water and oxygen, unlike transition metals such as nickel and copper.

q: In general, transition metals do not ____ readily in the atmosphere.
e: Most transition metals are resistant to atmospheric corrosion.

q: But ____ is an exception; it rusts easily.
e: Iron is a notable exception among transition metals because it rusts easily in the atmosphere.

q: Iron combined with non-metal carbon produces an alloy called ____.
e: Alloying iron with carbon produces steel.

q: Most transition elements form ____ compounds, whereas Groups 1 and II metals form white compounds.
e: The presence of incomplete d orbitals allows transition metals to form coloured compounds.

q: Most of them can form ions with different charges, so the transition elements show variable ____ states.
e: Transition elements exhibit variable oxidation states due to the involvement of both s and d electrons in bonding.

q: Most transition elements can form ____ ions.
e: Transition metals have a strong tendency to form complex ions with various ligands.

q: Compared to 3d series transition metals, alkali metals have a ____ melting point.
e: Alkali metals have low melting points compared to the high melting points of transition metals.

q: Transition elements typically have incompletely filled d orbitals or readily give rise to ions with partially filled ____ orbitals.
e: The defining characteristic of transition elements is their partially filled d orbitals.

q: These elements usually lose the electron from the ____ orbital first, which is followed by the removal of an electron from the d orbitals.
e: Ionization occurs by removing s-orbital electrons before d-orbital electrons.

q: The ____ oxidation states are more stable at the beginning of the series, i.e., the left side of Mn.
e: Higher oxidation states like +3 are more stable for the early 3d transition elements.

q: Towards the end of the series, i.e., the right side of Mn, ____ oxidation states are more stable.
e: Lower oxidation states like +2 become more stable towards the end of the 3d series.

q: The elements in the ____ of the series exhibit more oxidation states than those to the left or right.
e: Elements like manganese and iron in the middle of the series show the maximum number of oxidation states.

q: The highest oxidation state is ____ for manganese ($^{25}Mn$).
e: Manganese can exhibit a maximum oxidation state of +7, as seen in the permanganate ion.

q: The ions of chromium, manganese, and iron with the highest oxidation states tend to be good ____ agents.
e: Ions in their highest oxidation states are strong oxidising agents because they readily gain electrons.

q: Vanadium and chromium ions with the lowest oxidation state of +2 are good ____ agents.
e: Ions in low oxidation states like +2 act as reducing agents because they can easily be oxidized further.

q: Transition metals usually have their highest oxidation states in compounds with high ____ elements such as oxygen and fluorine.
e: Highly electronegative elements like oxygen and fluorine can stabilize the highest oxidation states of transition metals.

q: The colour of transition metal compounds is due to the presence of incomplete d orbitals or the presence of ____ electrons.
e: Unpaired d electrons allow for d-d transitions that absorb visible light and produce colour.

q: The transition metal compounds form coloured ions in an aqueous solution because they absorb part of the visible light and transmit the ____ colour.
e: The observed colour is the complementary colour of the wavelength of light absorbed by the ion.

q: $Sc^{3+}$ and $Zn^{2+}$ ions are ____ because $Sc^{3+}$ ion has completely empty d orbitals, and $Zn^{2+}$ has completely filled d orbitals.
e: Without partially filled d orbitals, d-d transitions cannot occur, making these ions colourless.

q: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are unpaired then it is a ____ substance.
e: Substances with unpaired electrons are attracted to magnetic fields and are paramagnetic.

q: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are paired, then it is a ____ substance.
e: Substances with only paired electrons are weakly repelled by magnetic fields and are diamagnetic.

q: Substances that are attracted very strongly by the applied magnetic field are said to be ____.
e: Ferromagnetic substances exhibit strong attraction to magnetic fields and can retain magnetization.

q: Iron, ____, and nickel are ferromagnetic substances.
e: Iron, cobalt, and nickel are the three main ferromagnetic transition elements.

q: Iron is used as a catalyst in the manufacture of ammonia in the ____ process.
e: Iron acts as a catalyst in the Haber process for synthesizing ammonia.

q: Vanadium is used in the form of vanadium(V) oxide in the manufacture of sulphuric acid in the ____ process.
e: Vanadium(V) oxide is the catalyst used in the Contact process for producing sulphuric acid.

q: Nickel is used as a catalyst in the ____ of alkenes.
e: Nickel catalyzes the addition of hydrogen to alkenes.

q: Titanium(IV) chloride ($TiCl_4$) is used for the manufacturing of high-density ____ in industries.
e: $TiCl_4$ acts as a Ziegler-Natta catalyst for producing high-density polyethene.

q: A complex ion is an ion, which has a metal ion at its centre with a number of other molecules or ions ____ it.
e: Complex ions consist of a central metal ion bonded to surrounding ligands.

q: A paramagnetic substance is a substance that has unpaired electrons and shows weak attraction towards the external ____ field.
e: Paramagnetism is characterized by weak attraction to an external magnetic field.

q: A diamagnetic substance is a substance that has no unpaired electrons and shows slight ____ from the external magnetic field.
e: Diamagnetic substances are slightly repelled by external magnetic fields.

q: A ferromagnetic substance is strongly attracted by the applied magnetic field, and retains its ____ for some time even after the external magnetic field is removed.
e: Ferromagnetic materials can retain their magnetization after the external field is removed.
